Hayley Metcalfe, 37, from Runcorn in Cheshire, said she and her husband Mike were "over the moon" to find out she was pregnant with her second son in 2023. But what followed was three years of heartbreak when Hayley suffered a placental abruption at 19 weeks pregnant and was told her baby boy, who they had named Oscar, had died. The following year, the couple lost a second baby, who they had named Leo, at 17 weeks pregnant. "The road after baby loss is never easy and trusting again can feel impossible," said Hayley. "But I want people to know there can still be hope." Image source, Handout Image caption, Hayley and Mike Metcalfe had their youngest child Hope via C-section in February Hayley said the couple had always wanted to start a family and, in 2019, the pair welcomed their eldest son George. She recalled how she had a normal pregnancy with George so when she fell pregnant again in 2023, her and husband Mike were excited to grow their family. But at 19 weeks and four days into her pregnancy, Hayley said she felt as though "something wasn't right". An ultrasound later confirmed that Oscar had died. "It sounds awful, but when you know your baby is no longer alive, you just want it all to be over," she said. "We already had so many baby things at home. "I just couldn't bear to look at them. title: Mum's says painful condition 'overlooked' during pregnancy

input.lead: Grace, 28, has spoken out about her traumatic pregnancy in the hope others do not suffer the same ordeal
input.summary: Grace, 28, has spoken out about her traumatic pregnancy in the hope others do not suffer the same ordeal
input.evidence_text: A mum who suffered from pre-eclampsia during pregnancy said she felt her symptoms were "overlooked" due to her underlying sickle cell disease Grace, 28, from Manchester, was in her second trimester when she started noticing how "physically taxing" her pregnancy had become including "extreme pain" It was only when she was admitted to St Mary's Hospital in Manchester with a sickle cell disease (SCD) unit that she was diagnosed with pre-eclampsia, a pregnancy-related condition that can cause high blood pressure, and went on to have an emergency Caesarean She has called for urgent research and more awareness of SCD so people do not suffer the same trauma ordeal she did She said: "It's not often you get pre-eclampsia present itself and not be flagged up "It was just something that was so overlooked that any symptom that was raised or any issue that was raised, they just put it down to sickle cell."

title: Why police are flying drones over Manchester's railway tracks

input.lead: The remotely operated aircraft can patrol lines for trespassers, reducing potential train delays
input.summary: The remotely operated aircraft can patrol lines for trespassers, reducing potential train delays
input.evidence_text: Police drones are being launched remotely over railway lines in Manchester as part of a scheme aimed at finding trespassers and reducing delays The aircraft are kept in weatherproof boxes at sites beside the railway and can be launched remotely by pilots based in London when an incident is reported Since the British Transport Police (BTP) launched its first site in Leeds in April 2025, four sites have been introduced across south London, as well as sites in Leicester and Manchester The BPT said Manchester was chosen because it is a known hotspot for trespass and disruption A pilot does not need to be on or near the site before the drone can take off, and the drone can also be used proactively - to patrol areas where intelligence suggests trespassing may be taking place BTP hopes to establish further sites in the North West as it expands the programme, although no additional locations have been announced so far

Mother-of-four Jacinta Batalha, 35, from Little Hulton, Salford, was awoken at 03:00 BST on 10 August by her son's shouts and was horrified to see someone stealing her car. She and her family then drove to an address 30 miles away in Blackburn, where the app said the car was. "I was so shocked," Batalha said, adding a DVLA check revealed the plates were for a Volkswagen. Later that day, the app revealed another location 20 minutes away in Colne, where she saw the car and recognised her belongings inside. She got inside and decided to drive off in case the thief returned to it. input.lead: International singers including Ariana Grande and Nelly Furtado have performed at Manchester Pride
input.summary: International singers including Ariana Grande and Nelly Furtado have performed at Manchester Pride
input.evidence_text: How Manchester Pride evolved from a bring-and-buy sale - BBC News Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Pride in Manchester began in 1985 from very humble beginnings By Darren Milby Radio Manchester Published 23 August 2026 Manchester Village Pride may look and feel familiar this year but a lot has changed over the past 12 months. The annual event, held over the August bank holiday weekend, hit the headlines in October 2025 when the company behind it went into voluntary administration. Manchester Pride Events LTD owed more than £1m to suppliers and performers. Many of these have still not been paid and the Charity Commission has launched an investigation into the organisation's finances. But how did Manchester Pride reach this point and what does the future hold? Pride in Manchester began in 1985 from very humble beginnings and grew into one of Europe's largest LGBTQ+ festivals attracting more than 170,000 visitors. Big names from the pop world such as Ariana Grande and Nelly Furtado have graced the stage and huge corporate brands were queuing up to have their logos associated with the weekend-long event. This is a world away from the very first Manchester Pride. Image source, Stuart Rhoades Image caption, For more than 40 years, people have gathered in Manchester for the annual event It started with a bring-and-buy sale on Canal Street in the city's Gay Village in 1985. The aim was to raise funds for the ward at Monsall Hospital in north Manchester that was treating patients at the height of the HIV and Aids crisis. The ward looked drab and depressing so fundraisers used the money raised to transform the unit into a welcoming space for patients and their families. input.evidence_text: The jobs of all 25 employees at Manchester kosher bakery State Fayre, whose roots dat e back to 1905 , have been saved after a sale secured its future State Fayre Ltd, which acquired the bakery business on Middleton Road, Crumpsall, in 2017, was wound up and placed into creditors’ voluntary liquidation earlier this month following sustained financial pressures These included soaring energy prices, significant increases in the cost of food and other raw materials, and higher payroll costs resulting from increases in the national minimum wage Steven Wiseglass, director and founder of insolvency and corporate recovery firm Inquesta, was appointed as liquidator and has secured the sale of the bakery’s trade, assets, brand and goodwill to YF & SF Bakery Ltd, a new company established by former State Fayre Ltd director Ye The sale enables the bakery to continue trading , with all 25 employees transferring to the new business under TUPE regulations. input.evidence_text: Bolton Council is launching a new licensing scheme for landlords of houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) The scheme is designed to improve property conditions, strengthen management standards, and ensure tenants have access to safe, high-quality accommodation and was agreed at a meeting of Bolton Council’s Cabinet on Monday (August 17) HMOs are properties that are occupied by three or more people from different households, who share at least one basic amenity i.e. a kitchen, bathroom or toilet - the definition includes bedsits, shared houses and some self–contained flats that did not meet the required standard It is unacceptable that landlords cut corners in critical areas such as failing to obtain fire, gas, and electrical safety certificates or ensuring properties are safe Many landlords operate responsibly, but a substantial proportion of HMOs are poorly managed, unsafe and impact on the community In the past three years, the council has received 1,885 complaints about disrepair in rented homes, typically relating to fire safety, electrical and structural defects, overcrowding, cold and damp, and poor waste management and pest control
